items.title: Lead Columbia-Class SSBN Recovers From Delay Risks
items.summary: During the Naval Submarine League Annual Symposium, Vice Admiral Rob Gaucher announced that the lead Columbia-class submarine, USS District of Columbia, has pulled back from severe delay risks that threatened a slip beyond 2030. By doubling weekly work hours and implementing 24-hour shift operations, the program has stabilized and targeted pressure-hull completion for 2027.

lines: The U.S. Space Force picked three firms for Phase I prototype agreements worth approximately $10 million total.

sections.label: Context
lines: Sep 2021: Air Force Space Systems Command issues initial sources-sought notice (SP-2020-05) for the Space Electromagnetic Warfare Operating Location (SEWOL) concept.
25 Jun 2024: Space Force outlines SEWOL contracting and fielding strategy, projecting Block 0/Initial Operational Capability and integration with systems like Meadowlands.

24 Jul 2025: Space Systems Command releases a formal Request for Information (RFI) and draft Statement of Work for SEWOL minimum viable products, targeting remote operations of systems like the Remote Modular Terminal (RMT) and Counter Communications System (CCS).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Moving from the initial 2021 concept and 2025 RFI stages, the Space Force is now prototyping cloud-based command software under an agile acquisition pathway, signaling a shift toward rapid commercial software integration.

items.title: U.S. Air Force Details $12.6B Plan for Palletized Cruise Missiles on Cargo Aircraft
items.summary: Air Force leadership detailed a budget request of $355 million for 1,000 FAMM-P rounds and a five-year plan for 28,000 missiles valued at $12.6 billion.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Air Force leadership detailed a budget request of $355 million for 1,000 FAMM-P rounds and a five-year plan for 28,000 missiles valued at $12.6 billion.

sections.label: Context
lines: Dec 2019: Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Strategic Development Planning and Experimentation (SDPE) office established the Rapid Dragon campaign to explore airdropping palletized cruise missiles from unmodified cargo aircraft.
Nov 2022: The Rapid Dragon concept saw its first operational deployment in Europe during exercise ATREUS 22 over the Norwegian Sea using an MC-130J.
2025: Congress granted a five-year acquisition and authorization framework for low-cost mass missile prototyping and procurement under the FY 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA).
Apr 2026: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) formally designated the palletized effort as program of record "Dragon Cart".

15 Jul 2026: The Pentagon announced framework agreements with Anduril Industries, CoAspire, and Zone 5 Technologies to develop and validate the Family of Affordable Mass Missiles (FAMM) under seven-year multi-year structures (Agreement).
25 Sep 2026: Anduril’s Barracuda family became the Air Force's first large-scale production munition certified compliant with Weapon Open System Architecture (WOSA) standards for FAMM integration.

6 Nov 2026: Air Force leadership formally briefed the capability shift at the Airlift/Tanker Association symposium, detailing a fiscal 2027 budget request of $355 million for 1,000 FAMM-P rounds and a five-year plan of 28,000 missiles valued at $12.6 billion (USD 12.6 billion).

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — 2026 National Defense Strategy (2026-01-23): Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.

US — PAC-3 MSE framework agreement under the Acquisition Transformation Strategy (2026-01-06): Seven-year framework agreements for proven munitions, giving industry long-term demand so it invests in capacity; PAC-3 MSE output to rise from about 600 to about 2,000 a year, subject to Congress.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following initial 2019 experiments and operational deployments, the program transitioned into the Dragon Cart program of record and multi-year industry frameworks, signaling a broader shift toward affordable mass munitions.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: FAMM Integration depends on Open-architecture guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) boards and WOSA-compliant seeker domains.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense suppliers should align component development with open-architecture WOSA standards to capture upcoming multi-year production opportunities.

items.title: Australian Firms Secure US Submarine Contracts and Train Locally
items.summary: ASC personnel who trained in Hawaii have returned to Australia to support the Submarine Maintenance Period for USS Colorado at HMAS Stirling. WA-based VEEM has secured purchase orders to supply specialized components to Huntington Ingalls Industries' Newport News Shipbuilding for US Navy Virginia-class submarines.

sections.label: What happened
lines: ASC personnel who trained in Hawaii have returned to Australia to support the Submarine Maintenance Period for USS Colorado at HMAS Stirling. WA-based VEEM has secured purchase orders to supply specialized components to Huntington Ingalls Industries' Newport News Shipbuilding for US Navy Virginia-class submarines.

sections.label: Context
lines: 15 Sep 2021: Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States announced the creation of the AUKUS trilateral security partnership, initiating plans for Australia to acquire nuclear-powered attack submarines (Agreement).
8 Feb 2022: The Exchange of Naval Nuclear Propulsion Information Agreement (ENNPIA) entered into force, enabling the trilateral sharing of restricted naval nuclear propulsion data (Agreement).
13 Mar 2023: AUKUS leaders announced the "Optimal Pathway" at San Diego, outlining the phased rollout of rotational submarine forces starting in 2027 and future delivery of SSN-AUKUS submarines.
Jul 2023: The Australian Submarine Agency (ASA) was officially established to oversee the acquisition, delivery, and sustainment of Australia's nuclear-powered submarine fleet.

8 Aug 2024: The formal agreement between the US, UK, and Australia for cooperation related to naval nuclear propulsion was submitted and published, cementing legal frameworks for technology transfer (Agreement).
15 Aug 2024: Australian civilian maintenance technicians began hands-on integration training at U.S. naval shipyards to prepare for sovereign submarine maintenance roles.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — NSPM: Rebuilding the United States Navy and America's Shipbuilding Industrial Base (2026-08-13): Fix long-term problems in Navy shipbuilding and repair: a fifth Naval shipyard, a submarine Component Repair Center, reorganisation of NAVSEA and direct investment in shipyards on the 'Finland model'.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the 2021 AUKUS announcement and subsequent establishment of maintenance and training frameworks, Australian industry is actively integrating into the US submarine supply chain ahead of the 2027 SRF-West rotational presence.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense supply chain and procurement professionals should monitor Australian suppliers entering US submarine programs as sovereign industrial capabilities expand under AUKUS.

items.title: Canada's JEF Membership Bid Undecided

sections.label: Context
lines: 5 Sep 2014: The Joint Expeditionary Force is formally launched as a UK initiative under NATO’s Framework Nations Concept at the Wales Summit.

items.title: France to Procure 20 Swedish CB90 Boats
items.summary: Following operational evaluations with loaned Swedish vessels in 2025, France is moving to procure 20 CB90 combat boats from Sweden via a government-to-government agreement to replace the stalled domestic VFM program.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Following operational evaluations with loaned Swedish vessels in 2025, France is moving to procure 20 CB90 combat boats from Sweden via a government-to-government agreement to replace the stalled domestic VFM program.

sections.label: Context
lines: 2023: French domestic VFM (Vedettes de Fusiliers Marins) Intercepteur 15 program runs into severe industrial difficulties, resulting in only two units delivered (Bir Hakeim and Laffaux) before the program is effectively halted (Delivered).

30 Jul 2025: The French Navy receives three CB90 fast patrol boats loaned by the Swedish Navy for an operational evaluation, deploying them to the Brest naval base (Amyot d'Inville Battalion) and Toulon (Détroyat Battalion).

20 May 2026: Reports emerge from European trade press (La Lettre, Militarnyi) indicating that a prospective defense-industrial swap or offset arrangement is being discussed, linking Sweden's acquisition of French Naval Group FDI frigates to a potential French procurement of Saab CB90 boats.

12 Nov 2026: The Swedish government submits a supplementary budget proposal to the Riksdag requesting authorization to negotiate and finalize a government-to-government contract in 2027 to sell up to 20 CB90 combat boats, crew training, and support equipment to France (Contract).
13 Nov 2026: French specialized defense media extensively detail the upcoming acquisition of 20 units by the Marine nationale to equip FORFUSCO.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: After the domestic VFM program stalled in 2023, the French Navy evaluated Swedish CB90 boats in 2025, leading the Swedish government to request parliamentary authorization in late 2026 to finalize a 20-unit procurement contract for France, signaling a pivot toward proven off-the-shelf Nordic platforms.

items.title: US Air Force Adopts Force Design 2026

sections.label: Context
lines: 3 May 2024: Air Force outlines plans to stand up the Integrated Capabilities Command to consolidate capability requirements under a single force design (Plan).

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — 2026 National Defense Strategy (2026-01-23): Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.

items.title: UK joins Norway’s P1118 vessel program for Royal Navy motherships

lines: Dec 2025: UK and Norway sign the wider Lunna House Agreement, setting the stage for industrial and naval cooperation including prospective UK integration into Norway’s vessel programmes (Agreement).
22 Jan 2026: Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (NDMA) initiates prequalification for the P1118 design competition covering up to 28 modular vessels.
30 Mar 2026: NDMA selects Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace and Salt Ship Design consortium to develop the concept and basic design for the P1118 standardised platform family.

items.title: Lockheed Martin reports rising foreign demand for PrSM amid output scale-up
items.summary: Lockheed Martin confirmed that foreign requests and export interest for the Precision Strike Missile are sharply accelerating as the company plans for increased manufacturing output.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Lockheed Martin confirmed that foreign requests and export interest for the Precision Strike Missile are sharply accelerating as the company plans for increased manufacturing output.

sections.label: Context
lines: Mar 2019: U.S. Army initiates post-INF treaty development posture for long-range surface-to-surface fires, targeting operational status for PrSM within four years.
16 Apr 2025: U.S. Army publishes Fiscal Year 2026 budget estimates showing structured procurement lines for PrSM, including multi-hundred unit quantities requested.

7 Jul 2026: United Kingdom commits GBP 190 million (~USD 254 million) from its Defence Investment Plan to officially join the U.S.–Australia PrSM joint development and procurement programme, aiming for first British deliveries in 2027 (Plan).

23 Jul 2026: Lockheed Martin CEO Jim Taiclet discloses company strategy to transition older ATACMS production overseas to Rheinmetall in Germany, freeing roughly two-thirds of the Camden, Arkansas manufacturing footprint exclusively for scaling PrSM output.
27 Oct 2026: Lockheed Martin showcases the PrSM Increment 4 (Long-Range Maneuverable Fires / ramjet variant) prototype designed to achieve ranges exceeding 1,000 km against maritime and land targets.

2026: Lockheed Martin executive leadership announces an overarching capital expenditure of over $8 billion through 2030 to expand missile manufacturing space by 2 million square feet across eight sites (including Troy, Alabama and Grand Prairie, Texas) to accelerate PrSM, PAC-3, and THAAD production.

12 Nov 2026: Lockheed Martin publicly confirms that foreign requests and export interest for PrSM are sharply accelerating alongside plans for higher manufacturing output enabled by digital engineering and computer-controlled machining partnerships (such as Hadrian).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Driven by long-range precision fire modernization priorities and multi-hundred unit procurement lines, the PrSM program has expanded from its initial U.S. Army development posture into a joint international framework involving Australia and the United Kingdom, supported by an over $8 billion capital expenditure through 2030 to scale multi-site missile manufacturing.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense supply chain and procurement professionals should monitor component lead times and digital machining integration partnerships as manufacturing capacity expands to meet international demand.
